title: Garry Nolan's magnesium-bismuth sample from Ubatuba
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Garry Nolan's magnesium-bismuth sample from Ubatuba, about 1950s-1960s at Ubatuba, Brazil; Stanford, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Gary Nolan has this magnesium bismuth piece in his lab at Stanford.

related.note: The same magnesium-bismuth piece in Nolan's Stanford lab, but this telling attributes it to Ubatuba, Brazil, where the story says it came from Roswell.

plain: Jesse Michels, a podcast host, says that Garry Nolan, a scientist at Stanford University, keeps a piece of metal made of magnesium and bismuth in his lab. The piece is said to come from Ubatuba, a coastal town in Brazil, linked to a reported UFO event in the 1950s or 1960s. If it came from such a craft, it would be physical material from something not made by people.
